brief: Ahead of Take-Two's 2FQ27 print, Goldman Sachs reiterates Buy and a $285 price target (38.8% upside), trimming the EV/GAAP EBITDA multiple to 33.0x from 35.0x and EV/FCF-SBC to 35x from 40x while raising estimates enough to hold the target flat. On GTA VI (releasing November 19th), GS argues pre-order units are not a valid demand proxy because digital distribution replaced the physical pre-order incentive that drove GTA V comparisons; Google Search and trailer viewership instead point to GTA VI as likely one of the largest AAA releases ever. GS frames FY27 bookings as conservative: implied GTA VI downloads of $1.9bn imply 34mm units, about 27% of a 125mm+ addressable install base, a figure GS calls likely overstated versus install base growth through CYE26; GS makes no estimate revisions yet, awaiting post-launch proof points. Beyond FY27, investor focus shifts to PC/online release timing (unannounced) and a 29-title FY27-29 pipeline, where specific titles matter more than quantity. NBA 2K27's lower review score points to a double-digit unit decline versus 2K26, while Red Dead Redemption and Borderlands show steadier growth. Industry data is mixed: the overall U.S. market fell 9% YoY in August even as Twitch and Steam engagement metrics were mostly positive.
